note: On starting point he is the closest thing in this batch to the stated ideal. A 1,002-day running streak, 12,000 to 20,000 steps a day, whole-food eating at 1,800-2,200 calories, no fast food, quit smoking, minimal alcohol — 'I'm consistent with everything else, but not this' — and his ask is explicitly incremental: 'I just want to get in better shape than I am, be toned up.' That is good to great, and he is emphatically not the fifty-pounds-overweight gym-averse exclusion. He also passes the affordability test on his own words: 'Do I have the money? Yeah, of course I have the money.' Where he falls outside is occupation. The stated ICP names business owners and physicians; he works in a retail store, and the money is real but already committed to a house under construction and an emergency fund. That is the interesting result: he failed on willingness, not capacity, and the ICP's income criterion — which tests affordability — would have passed him. The criterion that would actually have predicted this outcome is not in the stated ICP at all. Nor is the clinical one: he carries unhealed slipped discs at six to seven out of ten, and nothing in the stated criteria touches whether a body can perform loaded ballistic work.
